footer: Built client-side with Vite + React. Hosted as a static site — there is no server to receive your images.
aboutP1: ImgCompressor is a privacy-first image tool. It runs entirely in your browser — there is no server that receives, stores or analyses your photos.
aboutP2: Compression uses the Canvas API and WebAssembly codecs (MozJPEG, WebP, AVIF, OxiPNG) on your own device. That is why it works offline once loaded, and why there is no account or upload step.
aboutP3: This project is a static site. Hosting it costs almost nothing, because the heavy work is done by the visitor's browser, not by a server.
privacyP1: We do not collect, upload, store or share your images. Every file you drop stays on your device and is processed locally.
privacyP2: We do not use analytics, advertising trackers or accounts in this build. Your settings (theme and language) are saved only in your browser's localStorage.
privacyP3: If you deploy this project yourself and add analytics or a contact form later, update this page before you publish — do not claim 'no tracking' while tracking.
termsP1: ImgCompressor is provided as-is, free to use, for compressing images you have the right to use.
termsP2: You are responsible for your files. Do not use this tool to process illegal content, or to strip metadata from images you do not own or have permission to edit.
termsP3: Because processing is local, we cannot recover a file you delete, and we are not liable for quality loss from lossy compression. Keep your originals if they matter.
faqQ1: Do my images get uploaded anywhere?
faqA1: No. Compression runs 100% in your browser. You can test this by turning off your internet after the page loads — compression still works.
faqA2: WebP is the best balance of size and compatibility. AVIF is smaller but slower to encode. JPEG is best for photos when compatibility matters most, PNG for graphics and transparency.
faqQ3: Why is a format missing from the list?
faqA3: Only formats your current browser can actually encode are shown. This is checked at runtime with a small canvas test, so there is no silent fallback.
faqA4: Yes, after the first load the PWA can work offline. WASM codecs for a format are downloaded the first time you use that format.
